text: — Oh! Bai Ganyo, Christ is risen! Were you in the palace at the funeral?

"Who, me? Well, if it's not me, who will it be?" answers Bai Ganyo, and as he twists his left mustache, he gives me a sly look, meaning: "As long as there's a fool in the world, Bai Ganyo, don't you let your mouth be filled with gossip."
"So, how was it? Did you have fun?"

"And who's looking at you cheerfully, there was a rich man! I cut myself like... so-and-so... You know, Passion Sunday, I fasted, fasted, puffed myself up with these empty beans, and the army on top of that, I was as hungry as a cot. On Saturday I didn't put a crumb in my mouth. So they took it that they put the fast at two o'clock in the morning... While I was standing in church, it was as if three hundred leeches were sucking on my stomach. You spit, spit and there was no spit left. You say to stop it - don't go, it's bitter in your mouth... They said 'Christ is risen' - it's twelve o'clock, how can you wait until two o'clock! I told my family to go and break their fast alone, so I went into the Red Crab. There, my brother, it's full of people like me - top hats, epaulets, orders. And they're waiting for two o'clock to strike. I sat down at a long table, I see a few beggars breaking their fast. They laid out that table for me with snacks, pigs, and Varna wine on top — to drip down your stomach. Just looking at the skin of the piglet would have made me lose my mind. Well, what, I should have asked those bekjaers: "What are you eating there? Pig? Bravo! Ya... so-so... a little bit with skin..." — and they would have given me the people. But no. I've been shy since I was a child... (Give me your cigarette case, you smoke good tobacco, Ivanov's is no good at it, it smells like a hog...) Those bekjaers made me laugh, I got tired of looking at them, so I turned my eyes away. I said I should spit, but there was saliva! My intestines were stuck together. I thought about ordering a beer, so I scolded myself. That's why I've been starving, they say, for two days... I turned away so I wouldn't look at them, but they, as if on purpose, the devil take them, keep chewing and keep praising the pig. I wanted to get up, you know, to snatch that empty pig from their mouth... If only I could bend over, squeeze my stomach like that - I don't feel so hungry, but I can't bend over. My tailcoat is tight, it's going to bloom on my back. Come on, let the fog take it! And the starched collar, so hard that it scraped my neck like a saw... It's getting dark in my eyes. I left the Cancer, headed for the palace. You don't want to come in early. I have a friend of the Gavazian, a good friend at that, even if you ask, he's almost like a relative of mine, but he still doesn't give a damn. And even if you come in early, it doesn't matter, they won't set a table for you right away. I walked around, walked around the gates, my legs hurt. At one point, drrr... one python, after a while drrr... another python. They entered the palace, thank God! I curled my mustache, coughed and followed them. I went inside, I see the guards, the convoy, already lined up. A shaved boy rushed to take off my coat, I scolded him: "Excuse me, sir, mind your own business there," and I didn't let him undress me. He was ashamed and went to undress others. How can I let him undress me, brother? The sleeves of my coat, that is, not the sleeves, but the lining on the inside, were torn like... something. No way. I went upstairs, but before I went up, I took a look in the lower rooms - the tables were neatly laid out. A crowd gathered. We waited here for a while and the prince and princess came out. This time they had Christianly made a master and mistress. They gave us each an egg...

"Well, Helbetya... And I would kiss a hundred hands for such a meal. No way. That's the trouble, too, that when we fell down the stairs, my brother... If you want, believe me, if you want, no, I was throwing myself down three steps, I was about to hit the mirror, but I didn't let anyone beat me. I got my hands on the caviar, and when I dipped my spoon in, if it was less than half a kilo - it would be a sin on my soul. That fish mayonnaise, those snacks, I don't know their names, when those mouths of mine were gaping... Stop it!... I ate, ate, ate... and to this day I wonder how my stomach didn't burst." What about drinking... When did I leave, how did I leave - I can't remember... Ugh!... My head still hurts from all that empty champagne... Leave that alone, when I took it, when I stuffed my pockets with pasties, and the soft ones, the devil take them, when they got smeared in my pocket... Well, let's say goodbye.
